subsystems.name: Qubit platform
subsystems.role: the quantum bits whose coherence we want to extend.
parts: superconducting circuits or trapped ions or spin defects

subsystems.name: Metamaterial structure
subsystems.role: engineered to shape the electromagnetic environment at the qubit's operating frequency.

subsystems.name: Cryogenic and vacuum system
subsystems.role: keeps the qubits at millikelvin temperatures and free of stray molecules.

subsystems.name: Control and readout electronics
subsystems.role: manipulates and measures the qubit states.

subsystems.name: Integration and packaging
subsystems.role: brings metamaterial and qubit into a single, stable device.

subsystems.name: Metrology and characterization
subsystems.role: measures coherence times and identifies remaining noise.

buildSteps.title: Identify decoherence sources
buildSteps.detail: Analyze the qubit's environment to find the dominant noise, such as dielectric loss, magnetic flux noise or thermal photons.

buildSteps.title: Design the metamaterial
buildSteps.detail: Use electromagnetic simulation to create a structure that filters or redirects noise at the qubit frequency while allowing control signals to pass.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the metamaterial
buildSteps.detail: Deposit and pattern thin films of superconductors and dielectrics using lithography and etching to form sub-wavelength elements.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the qubits
buildSteps.detail: Make the qubit circuits on a separate chip or monolithically, using established quantum device fabrication.

buildSteps.title: Integrate metamaterial and qubits
buildSteps.detail: Align and bond the metamaterial to the qubit chip, ensuring minimal parasitic modes and no interference with wiring.

buildSteps.title: Cool and characterize
buildSteps.detail: Cool the assembly in a dilution refrigerator and measure coherence times (T1, T2) with and without the metamaterial.

buildSteps.title: Optimize and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Adjust metamaterial geometry and materials to maximize coherence while preserving gate speed and fidelity.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate multi-qubit operation
buildSteps.detail: Show that the metamaterial improves a small processor, not just a single qubit, without introducing crosstalk.

buildSteps.title: Scale and integrate with control electronics
buildSteps.detail: Ensure the metamaterial remains compatible with dense wiring and readout as the qubit count grows.

prerequisites.why: superconducting qubits reach tens to hundreds of microseconds, but need improvement for large-scale systems.
metamaterials are made for optics and microwaves, but not yet tailored for qubit environments.
dilution refrigerators are standard in quantum computing labs.
many noise sources are known, but their relative contributions vary by platform.

pathway.milestone: research on metamaterials for electromagnetic filtering and shielding in quantum devices
pathway.unlocks: proof-of-principle that engineered materials can reduce specific noise.

pathway.milestone: demonstration of extended coherence in a single qubit using an integrated metamaterial
application to multi-qubit processors without harming gate fidelity
pathway.unlocks: a practical route to more reliable quantum computation.

pathway.milestone: metamaterials as standard components in quantum processors
